reactiveHandler.name: KasuwaReactiveHandler.sol
reactiveHandler.note: Redeployed here after the original address (0x9D60C436CCD13055EE4CeAb4b8E77d24c2CA5c02) was found to be an unused EOA with no deployment transaction. This new address is a real, confirmed contract creation.

deployerEOA.name: Deployer Wallet (EOA)
deployerEOA.note: This exact address was mistakenly passed as the _policyContract constructor argument to both KasuwaExecutor and KasuwaReactiveHandler at deploy time -- see policyContractWiring below.

policyContractWiring.description: Both KasuwaExecutor and KasuwaReactiveHandler take a _policyContract constructor argument that should point at the deployed KasuwaPolicy contract. Both were instead deployed pointing at the deployer's own wallet address -- a plain EOA with no contract code. This was caught by reading policyContract() live via Blockscout's Read Contract tab on KasuwaExecutor, and cross-checked against KasuwaReactiveHandler's recorded constructor argument.
policyContractWiring.actualWiredAddressType: EOA (no contract code) -- this is the deployer wallet, not KasuwaPolicy
policyContractWiring.practicalImpact: Any call that routes through IKasuwaPolicy(policyContract) -- KasuwaExecutor.executeAutoRoll() and the policy-side hooks in KasuwaReactiveHandler.onMarketSettled() -- will currently revert, because ABI-decoding a return value against an address with no code fails under Solidity 0.8.x.

remediation.kasuwaExecutor: Has an onlyOwner setPolicyContract(address) function. The deployer wallet can call setPolicyContract(0xAc8c3afB4f11b43E1C90fC57AEDc91e3e7140d1d) to fix this in place.
remediation.kasuwaReactiveHandler: policyContract is only ever set in the constructor -- there is no setter. Fixing this requires a fresh redeploy pointed at the correct KasuwaPolicy address.
